HALLMARK 14 · NARRATIVE WORKFLOW / BROADSIDE THEME
HOW TO SKATEBOARD: THE FOUR SKILLS
KNOW YOUR BOARD
Eight bolts anchor the trucks to the maple deck. The nose points in your direction of roll; the tail curves up to allow pop and clearance. Grip tape holds rubber soles firmly.
RULE ZERO: Always wear helmet, wrist guards, and pads before stepping on the grip. Flat rubber-soled skate shoes are non-negotiable.
1.0
FIND YOUR STANCE
Feet set across the width of the board, each foot resting directly over a set of truck bolts. Keep your knees flexed and center of mass low. Try this stationary on grass or carpet first so the wheels cannot roll out.
2.0
PUSH OFF
Turn your front foot to point straight forward toward the nose over the front bolts. Lower your hips and push steadily against the asphalt with your back foot. Once rolling, bring the back foot onto the tail bolts and pivot sideways.
3.0
LEAN TO TURN (CARVING)
Steering does not require lifting the board. Press weight into your toes to carve toe-side; lean gently into your heels to curve heel-side. The rubber bushings inside the metal trucks compress and steer the wheelbase.
4.0
FOOT BRAKE TO STOP
Do not jump off a moving board. Rotate your front foot parallel to the deck, gently take the back foot off, and drag the flat rubber sole along the ground with increasing friction until you come to a smooth, controlled halt.
